Hykmann Global Business Solutions AB is looking for an experienced Senior Maintenance Engineer for a challenging consulting assignment with an internationally renowned client in advanced engineering, testing, and research & development.
Are you passionate about maintenance engineering, electrical systems, automation, and troubleshooting complex technical equipment? This opportunity allows you to take responsibility for the reliability and performance of advanced test facilities used for research, development, testing, and verification.
We’re looking for a technically strong professional who can combine hands-on maintenance expertise with maintenance planning, continuous improvement, supplier coordination, and lifecycle management of equipment.

As a Senior Maintenance Engineer, you will plan, coordinate, and improve preventive and corrective maintenance across a variety of systems within an advanced R&D test facility containing multiple test cells.
You will work with electrical and automation equipment, test rigs, measurement systems, and supporting infrastructure. In addition to daily maintenance activities, you will contribute to larger technical projects, develop maintenance procedures, coordinate external service providers, and support cost optimization and equipment reliability.
This is a senior role that requires independent problem-solving, technical judgement, and the ability to manage complex maintenance activities with limited supervision.

Plan and coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance across test facility equipment and systems.
Troubleshoot faults and perform maintenance activities on technical equipment used in testing and verification.

Read and interpret flow diagrams, electrical drawings, technical manuals, and equipment documentation.
Plan and coordinate external service personnel and subcontractors.
Manage spare-parts requirements, service contracts, and maintenance-related purchasing.
Contribute to maintenance budgets, cost optimization initiatives, and continuous improvement activities.

Coach and support colleagues and contribute to the development of maintenance practices and technical competence.

✅ Required Skills & Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Typically more than 5 years of relevant maintenance engineering experience.
Experience planning, coordinating, monitoring, and improving maintenance operations.
Practical experience using maintenance management software or maintenance systems.
Strong technical understanding of electrical equipment, automation systems, and industrial or test facility infrastructure.
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, flow diagrams, equipment manuals, and technical specifications.
Experience with troubleshooting, fault analysis, preventive maintenance, and corrective maintenance.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a hands-on approach to technical challenges.
Ability to coordinate service providers, manage maintenance activities, and work independently.
Fluent Swedish and English, both written and spoken.

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be an advantage:
Maintenance and troubleshooting of equipment in test facilities, laboratories, or R&D environments.
Maintenance of production equipment or other technically complex industrial installations.
Dynamometer systems, test rigs, battery simulators, drive systems, or electrical test equipment.
PLC-based automation, instrumentation, measurement systems, and test infrastructure.

jobs.occupation: Become our next EPI Process engineer assistant
jobs.description:
SweGaN is a European semiconductor manufacturer that develops and produces customer-made materials and high-performance epitaxial wafers of gallium nitride for manufacturers of conductive components and devices. We develop and deliver unique material solutions based on the company's groundbreaking GaN epitaxial technology.
SweGaN's products are used for a wide range of applications, including 5G telecommunications infrastructure, defence radar, satellite communications, electric vehicles, high-voltage switches, and more. SweGaN's benchmark QuanFINE® epitaxial growth technology increases the performance of RF and power devices and reduces energy consumption.
About the role
As a Process Engineer Assistant at SweGaN, you will play an important supporting role within our Process Engineering team.
This is a varied position where you will combine hands-on wafer characterization and measurements with technical documentation, data management, and administrative coordination.
You will work closely with our process engineers and act as an important link between Process Engineering and Operations, helping to ensure that technical information, measurement results, and process-related activities are managed accurately and efficiently.
You will also have the opportunity to develop your technical skills and become qualified to operate relevant characterization and measurement equipment, both within SweGaN and through external facilities.
Responsibilities
Support process engineers in their daily work through practical, administrative, and coordinating activities.
Perform wafer characterization and measurements using relevant equipment, following established procedures and instructions.
Collect, register, verify, and compile process data and measurement results.
Maintain accurate technical documentation, process records, and traceability.
Work with ERP and maintenance management systems, including Monitor and MaintMaster.
Support the administration and follow-up of process-related activities and documentation.
Assist with quality documentation, including control plans, OCAP, SPC, and Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
Identify opportunities to improve administrative workflows, data quality, and documentation.
Coordinate information and activities between Process Engineering, Production, Maintenance, and Quality.
Contribute to continuous improvement and more efficient working methods.

What we are looking for
We are looking for a structured, detail-oriented, and technically curious person who enjoys making things work smoothly.
You appreciate accuracy, understand the importance of reliable data, and enjoy working with both technical equipment and administrative systems.
You take responsibility for your tasks, work independently when needed, and enjoy collaborating with colleagues across different departments.
You do not need to be an experienced process engineer. What matters is your willingness to learn, your practical understanding of industrial operations, and your ability to bring structure and quality to your work.
Requirements
Upper secondary education with a technical, industrial, or administrative focus, or equivalent relevant work experience.
Experience in production, industrial operations, technical administration, or a similar environment.
Good computer skills and experience working with business or production systems.
Good knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
A structured and accurate approach to documentation, data management, and follow-up.
An interest in technical measurements and a willingness to learn how to operate characterization equipment.
Good communication and collaboration skills.
Good written and spoken English.

Meritorious 
Experience working with Monitor ERP or MaintMaster.
A background in Production, Operations, or industrial manufacturing.
Experience with measurement equipment, laboratory work, or wafer characterization.
Basic knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing or process engineering.
Experience in technical documentation, quality systems, or deviation management.
Experience improving administrative processes and workflows.

Why join SweGaN?
At SweGaN, you will become part of a growing international team working with advanced semiconductor technology.
We offer a varied role where you can combine your practical and administrative skills while developing new technical competencies.
You will have the opportunity to work closely with experienced engineers, gain hands-on experience with advanced measurement equipment, and contribute to the structure and efficiency of our manufacturing operations.
Your work will make a difference by ensuring that our engineers have access to accurate information, reliable measurement data, and effective administrative support.
If you are a structured and technically curious problem solver who enjoys working hands-on with measurement equipment, organizing technical information, improving workflows, and supporting engineers in turning data into meaningful improvements, we encourage you to apply.

TL;DR: Most companies treat documentation as a help centre. At Lovable it's part of the product. Millions of people learn to build software from our docs, and so do the AI agents working for them: the Lovable agent suggests pages, coding tools read them, and our assistants answer from them. You'll be our second technical writer, with product areas of your own from the start and a seat at every launch, and you'll help work out something nobody has fully worked out yet: what documentation should be when its readers are people and agents, and the product changes every day.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.
We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What we're looking for
You've spent 3+ years documenting software products, and you can show us pages that get a reader to the outcome without re-reading.
You already write with AI: for research, drafting and checking, not just polish. You know what it gets wrong and you catch it.
You test what you document. You'd rather try the feature and read the source than take someone's word for it, and when something's broken or confusing, you say so.
You're at home in docs-as-code: Git, Markdown and pull requests.
You ask engineers and PMs specific questions, and when documenting a feature shows it won't make sense to users, you raise it early, with reasons.

Preferred:
You've shipped docs weekly at a startup or scale-up, finding out what changed yourself.
You've written for AI readers, or you're curious about it.
You have UX writing or content design experience, or an interest in it.
You can read code well enough to check how a feature actually behaves; writing code is not required.

What you'll do
Drive, don't wait. Features land every day, and bigger launches several times a month. You find out what's shipping before anyone tells you, and the docs are ready the day it ships.
Own it end to end. Work a feature out from the code and the product, write the page, verify it in Lovable, ship it, and keep it true as the product moves.
Care about the reader more than the feature. Our docs come with data: what people can't find, what the assistant couldn't answer, what support hears. You use it to decide what to write next.
Make the product better, not just explain it. Documenting a feature means using it end to end. You'll find the confusing label or the broken step and get it fixed before launch.
Write for three readers on one page. The non-technical builder, the developer, and the AI agent working on their behalf.
Build something that outlasts the week. AI drafts a lot of our pages. The human work is judgement: what a feature needs, what the engineer didn't mention, and the checks that keep hundreds of pages correct.

Where you'll start:
Enterprise. Identity and access, governance, audit, data residency: the pages a security team reads before they sign.
The developer surface. Take our API and MCP references from correct to complete.
Your first launch. Own the docs for one in your first weeks, from working group to launch day.
Your first automation. Pick one check we still do by hand and make it run on its own.

About your application
Please submit your application and your writing samples in English using the form below. It's our company language, so you'll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you're interested, please apply through our careers portal.

What we do at Blykalla
Blykalla is a global leader in advanced nuclear technology, commercialising the next generation of clean, reliable energy through its lead-cooled reactor, the SEALER. By combining decades of specialised research with world-class partners, Blykalla is building the backbone of the global AI and industrial economy. For more information, visit https://www.blykalla.com.

What you’ll get to do
We're seeking a Senior Thermal-Hydraulics Code Validation Engineer to join our Nuclear Engineering & Safety team, working from Stockholm or Oskarshamn. In this role, you will work on experiments with the aim of validating thermal-hydraulics system codes for use in the design and safety analysis of our lead-cooled fast reactors.

More specifically, you will
Coordinate, specify and analyze experiments to be run in our ARTS (Advanced Reactor Testing Site) facility in Oskarshamn.
Act as a technical lead for engineers and technicians working on both the experiments and the simulation codes.
Contribute to our validation program for thermal hydraulics system codes and associated methodologies.
Stay current with advances in thermal hydraulics, computational methods, and regulatory requirements.

Who you’ll get to work with
The thermal-hydraulics validation engineer sits in the Nuclear Engineering & Safety team within Blykalla, and reports to the manager of Nuclear Engineering & Safety. We are a diverse team that is passionate about our work and our company. You can choose to work from any of our offices in Stockholm, Oskarshamn or ARTS (at Simpevarp). In case of work from the Stockholm office, frequent (monthly) travel to the ARTS site is expected.
Who you are
You will be part of a highly skilled team with a can-do attitude. We value personal chemistry and strive to create a workplace where you enjoy coming to. There are however a few things that we think will help for you to succeed in this role, these are:
Master's degree in physics, engineering or a related field

A structured way of working, together with excellent problem-solving and technical writing skills
Fluency in English, spoken and written

Experience in supporting nuclear licensing activities or in regulatory interaction
Fluency in Swedish, spoken and written

Reference & Background Checks

We may also conduct reference checks to gain a well-rounded understanding of your professional experience, performance, and ways of working. This includes both references provided by you and, where relevant, conversations with other professional contacts who have worked closely with you. We are looking for an ambitious, commercially minded Finance Lead to join a fast-scaling AI company backed by NVIDIA, Microsoft, and AWS, and to grow with it.
About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP). Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
This is not a traditional accounting position. Half the job is making the financial foundation work exceptionally well: payroll, bookkeeping, tax, payments, reporting, and administration, together with our founders and external advisers. The other half is commercial: working with the founders on pricing, business models, cost structures, and where the company puts its money.
One day you might be running payroll and closing the month. The next, you could be modeling the economics of deploying our platform across hundreds of customer sites, finding a European innovation grant, or helping the CEO evaluate a new commercial opportunity.
What you will work on
• Bookkeeping, reconciliations, and monthly and annual closing in Fortnox.
• Payroll, benefits, reimbursements, VAT, and tax, together with our auditors and banks.
• Invoicing, supplier payments, accounts payable and receivable, and corporate cards (Mynt).
• Filings with Bolagsverket and Skatteverket, board materials, minutes, and shareholder documentation.
• Budgets, forecasts, cash flow and runway models, and reporting for leadership, the board, and investors.
• Unit economics across cloud, AI inference, hardware, and deployment, and the margins they produce.
• Grants and non-dilutive funding from Swedish and European programmes.
• Replacing repetitive finance work with AI and modern software, so the function scales without its overhead growing at the same rate.
Who we are looking for
You are early in your career, with a strong financial foundation and an appetite for far more responsibility than you have today. You might be at a Big Four or mid-sized audit firm, an accounting agency, or in finance operations at a growing company.
• Around 2–4 years in accounting, auditing, or financial operations.
• Solid command of Swedish bookkeeping, payroll, and compliance, and hands-on experience with Fortnox or similar.
• Strong analytical skills and a real interest in modeling and commercial analysis.
• Excellent Swedish and English, written and spoken.
You take responsibility for the outcome, not just the task. You know payroll and tax have to be right every time while almost everything else moves fast, and you can hold both. You do not wait to be asked before fixing a process or chasing an opportunity.
It is a plus if you have worked with startups or venture-backed companies, understand SaaS metrics and unit economics, or have applied for funding through Vinnova, Almi, or EU programmes. You do not need all of this. We care more about judgment and how fast you learn than about years on your CV.
Life at Antrino
You will join a team of driven, ambitious people who thrive at a fast pace and enjoy working together. We go to AI events, host our own, and end plenty of weeks with an afterwork. Things change quickly here, and everyone's work is visible in what the company becomes.
What we offer
• Direct work with the CEO and board members on financial and commercial decisions.
• Exposure to fundraising, investor relations, and international expansion.
• Potential participation in our stock option programme after the probationary period.
• Freedom to improve systems, challenge processes, and bring AI into finance work.
• AI events, afterworks, team activities, and travel when the business requires it.
• Occupational pension, insurance, and friskvårdsbidrag.
Process
1. Introductory conversation about your background and ambitions.
2. Finance and accounting conversation about your hands-on experience.
3. Practical working session on a realistic scenario in operations, forecasting, or a commercial decision. We care how you think.
4. Conversation with the founders about options and terms.
We review applications continuously. References may be requested at the final stage.
Apply with your CV and a short note on why you want to move beyond traditional accounting into helping build a technology company.

Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices for manufacturing systems. 

Highly autonomous with a proactive mindset and work ethic.  

Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment. 

Ability to document technical problems concisely. 

Experience in coaching, upskilling, and mentoring engineers or technicians, with a demonstrable commitment to developing the technical capability of others within a production environment.

Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments. 

A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.
